name: Executive Order of May 15, 1876 correctly defining the boundaries of the Colorado River reservation (Royce area 593)
nations: Colorado River Indian Tribes (Mohave, Chemehuevi, Hopi and Navajo)
promises: Not a cession: the President, alluding to previous errors, correctly defined the boundaries of the Colorado River reservation, from La Paz arroyo to Black Mountain, across the river to Monument Peak and Riverside Mountain in California, and back along the west bank (Royce p. 886). Royce refers to the Act of March 3, 1865 and the Executive orders of November 22, 1873 and November 16, 1874 (Royce p. 887).

Royce records that the boundaries of the November 16, 1874 order were found defective and incomplete, so that order was superseded by this one, "wherein the enlarged boundaries were correctly defined" (Royce p. 877).
landTaken: None by this order; it added land. The Indian Claims Commission dated the taking of Mohave lands outside the reservation to the Act of March 3, 1865 (Dockets 283 and 295), which is the separate record cession-1865-03-03-colorado-river.
today: The Colorado River Indian Tribes say the reservation, created in 1865, stretches along both banks of the river and includes almost 300,000 acres.

nationVoice.summary: CRIT says the reservation was created in 1865 for the Indians of the Colorado River, first the Mohave and Chemehuevi who had lived there for centuries, with Hopi and Navajo people relocated there later.

openQuestions: The dispute over the reservation's western (California) boundary under this order, litigated in Arizona v. California, was not researched; whether any ruling treats land inside these boundaries as taken was not checked.
The Mohave decision (id 283) was re-read in the round 13 audit: it concludes the Mohave were deprived of their lands in Arizona and Nevada on March 3, 1865 without compensation.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 13): first promise said the reservation was "enlarged in 1873 and 1874"; Royce p. 887 only cross-references the 1873 and 1874 orders, and p. 877 says this order correctly defined the enlarged boundaries. Reworded to Royce. Royce pp. 877, 886 and 887 checked on the page scans.

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Court of Claims "Colorado River" and "Mohave" (opened 156 Ct. Cl. 712, 221 Ct. Cl. 989, 222 Ct. Cl. 690, 203 Ct. Cl. 709) and ICC full text "Colorado River reservation 1876 boundary", "Colorado River Indian Tribes 1874"; no finding about this order. The 1962 order sent to the ICC a CRIT claim that the United States settled other tribes and persons on its lands from 1942 and 1945; a stipulated judgment of $850,000 was entered on October 19, 1979 (221 Ct. Cl. 989). That is a settlement about 1940s use, not a finding about this order.
